Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 10-May-2025 (09:30 AM - 12:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  SECOND SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - APRIL / MAY 2025  
  SUBJECT: CSE 1071/CSE_1071 - PROBLEM SOLVING USING COMPUTERS  
  PROBLEM SOLVING USING COMPUTERS [CSE 1071-CHM]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                 Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1A)               Draw a flowchart to find all the roots of a quadratic equation ax2 +bx+c=0.                          (3)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
1B)               Write a C program to assign grades based on marks using the conditional operator                     (3)  
  90 and above: A  
  75-89: B  
  60-74: C  
  Below 60: Fail  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
1C)               Write a C program to build a simple student grading system to calculate the final grade              (4)  
  based on the marks in different subjects (Using Else-If)  
  The program will:  
  1. Take marks for Math, Science, and English.  
  2. Calculate the total and average marks.  
  3. Determine the grade based on average marks using the following criteria:  
  • 90-100: A+  
  • 80-89: A  
  • 70-79: B+  
  • 60-69: B  
  • 50-59: C  
  • Below 50: Fail  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2A)               Write a C program to count the number of prime digits in a given number.                             (2)  
  For example:  
  • Input: Enter a number: 8902357  
  output: Number of prime digits: 4  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2B)               Write a C program to find the second largest element in an array of n integers.                      (4)  
  • Input: Number of elements n, followed by n integers.  
  • Output: The second largest number in the array.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  
  Page 1 of 4

2C)   Write a C program that Accepts an NxN matrix.                                                           (4)  
  Finds and prints the Sum of the main diagonal.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3A)   Write a function prototype for a function named processData that takes an array of integers and its (2)  
  size as parameters and returns the average of the array elements as a floating-point number.  
  Provide the function definition.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3B)   Write a function named calculateSum() that takes two integers as parameters and returns their           (4)  
  sum. Additionally, write another function named printSum() that takes two integers as parameters,  
  calls calculateSum(), and prints the result. Explain the scope of variables used in both functions  
  with the complete program.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3C)   Write a recursive function in C to calculate the sum of digits of a given non-negative integer. The     (4)  
  main () function must take the user input for a non-negative integer, call the recursive function and  
  print the sum in main ().  
  Sample I/O:  
  Enter a non-negative integer: 123  
  $$Sum of digits = 6$$  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4A)   Write a C program that adds the user's deposit amount to the bank balance amount and prints the         (3)  
  updated bank balance.  
  The program must do the following tasks:  
  • Accepts the bank balance and a deposit amount from the user.  
  • Call a function updateBalance(), which adds the deposit amount to the balance using pass-by-  
  reference.  
  • Display the balance before and after the deposit in  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4B)   Write a C program to rotate a mxn matrix 90 degrees clockwise. The program must do the following (4)  
  tasks.  
  i) Enter the size of the matrix and its elements. Print it in the matrix form.  
  ii) Call a function called rotate() in the main function. Perform 900 rotation and print the rotated  
  matrix in the rotate() function.  
  The sample input and output matrix are shown below.  
  
  
  Page 2 of 4

Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4C)   A university must identify the student with the highest average score across three subjects out of (3)  
  100 students.  
  Write a C program using a structure to store each student's name, roll number, and marks in three  
  subjects. Compute each student's average and display the student details with the highest average  
  score.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5A)   A hospital wants to monitor the condition of individual patients based on their vital signs and recent (3)  
  test results. Use nested structures and an array within a structure (but not an array of structures) to  
  store a single patient's health data.  
  Define a structure Vitals to store: Body temperature (in Fahrenheit), Heart rate (in beats per  
  minute), Oxygen level (percentage).  
  Define another structure, Patient, which includes Patient ID (integer), Patient name (string), a  
  nested Vitals structure, and an array of 5 floating-point numbers representing the test scores for the  
  last 5 months.  
  Write a C program to read all the above information for one patient, (ii) calculate the average test  
  scores, (iii) display the patient's full information only if the oxygen level is below 92% or the  
  average test score is less than 50.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5B)   Write a C program to accept an array of integer values. Print the odd numbers along with their         (4)  
  address in the reverse order using only pointers. The sample input and output are shown  
  below.
